title: Newly-elected Councilwoman Crystal Black speaks about addressing Bingham Park in Greensboro - NewsBreak
text:
By Justin Lundy Dolan Reynolds ,
3 hours ago
GREENSBORO, N.C. (WGHP) — A newly-elected Greensboro City Councilwoman is weighing in on the future of a Greensboro park.
Zahir Muhammad grew up near Bingham Park in Greensboro, which is now fenced off with no way inside.
He says It’s an eye soar to look at what’s happened to what was once the heart of the community.
“I think this might be the only basketball court in the area. It’s a big hassle on the kids not being able to go play basketball, not being able to have fun outside. Usually, this would be packed,” Muhammad said.
Last year, testing done by the city found high levels toxins in the park’s soil. This came over 70 years after the land was used as a landfill back in the 1950s.
The discovery lead to the closure of the property. Officials voted to cap and cover Bingham Park.
According to the City of Greensboro, it would cost $12.4 million to fix the park, and more than a foot of dirt would be laid out over the contaminated area.
The other option to fix the park was a full remediation, which would cost more than $39 million.
It’s an option newly-elected Greensboro City Councilwoman Crystal Black would like to re-evaluate.
“The cap and cover is a Band-Aid. Its kicking the can down the road. It would have to be addressed later on by another council. Maybe by another council decades into the future. I believe this community deserves to have a contaminated free space where kids can thrive and play. You can’t do that in a park that has a 12-inch layer of soil that you can’t plant or play on,” Black said.
The main reason some city council members voted for the cheaper option was because at the time, the city didn’t have enough state or federal funds to fully remediate the park.
Black says once she gets into office, she hopes to get the ball rolling in regards to funding the project.
“I will be working with my colleagues, private and public partners to have that conversation … I think grace needs to be given to allow us to meet and discuss and have those collaborations moving forward. What I can share with you is that my goal is to bring dignity back to the community and the Bingham Park residents,” Black said.
FOX8 reached out to newly-elected Mayor Marikay Abuzuaiter about her thoughts on the a full remediation of Bingham Park.
She says that right now, the best thing to do is move forward with the cap and cover, but she hopes the city will apply for federal and state funds to finally remediate the park.
